Definition: from G4862 and G2980; to talk together, i.e. converse:--commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.
BiblicalUsage: On the mount of transfiguration Moses and Elijah appear talking with Jesus, and in the dark of the same week Judas goes and communes with the chief priests about how to betray Him. The same word covers holy conversation and treacherous plotting, and the company you keep in your talk tells which it is.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that words spoken together shape what happens next, for good or for evil, so I want my conversations to be the kind heaven would join.
